source: SAD (Situational Awareness Dataset), Laine et al. 2024, arXiv 2407.04694, CC-BY 4.0
why_seed: One seed, fixed, so the draw is a fact about the spec rather than about when it was run.
why_n_per_set: Equal weight per set, not per item. Drawn in proportion to the pool, human_defaults' 899 items would be 56% of the battery and the set-level means would mostly be one set's mean. 80 is the largest round number every set but names can supply after drops; names takes all 50, since it is 50 rephrasings of a single question and sampling them would only discard rephrasings.
why_n_samples: Five repeats per item, so an item score is a frequency rather than a coin flip, and a within-item consistency read is available. SAD itself runs each item once and gets its stability from item count; we trade item count for repeats because a persona's stance is the thing that varies.
why_drop_rules: An item a nineteenth-century person and a model would answer identically cannot show displacement, so it costs a call and yields nothing. `unclear` and `unparsed` are dropped rather than pooled: a residual stratum made of items the labeller could not place is not a stratum, it is a mixture.
why_drop_rules_apply_to: Only these two sets were labelled, because only these two ship no stratification variable. Applying a drop rule to the other three would mean labelling them too, which would add a way to disagree with strata SAD already publishes.
why_strata_field: Each set is stratified on whatever variable it has: the labelled `axis` for the two that had none, SAD's own `subset` and `cat` for the two that do. `names` is unstratified because it has one question.
why_allocation: Equal share per stratum, capped at what a stratum holds, with the overflow redistributed among strata that still have room. Proportional allocation was tried first and rejected: it hands the draw's shape to whatever the benchmark happened to write most of, so human_defaults' 371 body questions would have taken 43 of its 80 places while its 15 AI-nature questions took 2 -- and 2 items cannot carry a score. Equal allocation asks each kind of question about as often as every other, which is what makes a per-kind reading possible at all. A stratum smaller than its equal share contributes everything it has and the rest is shared out, so no draw is held back by the scarcest kind.
why_stem: The parameters are in the filename, so two draws cannot be confused for one another on disk.
why_one_draw: There is no --subset. MMLU's builder slices a smaller set out of the full draw because its uids encode a rank; a SAD uid is the sha of the question and carries no position, so a smaller n would have to be a fresh stratified draw and would share only part of this one. If a smaller battery is ever wanted, it gets its own seed and its own stem rather than a slice that looks like this one.
